STEP 2 - Ruler: White disposable plate, about 20 cm in diameter (side-plate size). Area = 3.14 x (10)^2 ≈ 314 cm^2. The grey tray is about 35 cm wide, consistent with this plate size.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Lasagna (pasta layers, meat ragù, melted cheese) as one rectangular piece
- Paper cone (not food, the cone contents are not visible, so not counted)
- Water (not counted in energy)

STEP 4 - Area: Lasagna piece covers roughly 35% of the plate area (about 110 cm^2), since it is a squarish block about 10 x 11 cm on the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: 110 cm^2 x 3.5 cm average height (stacked layers) ≈ 385 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: Lasagna is dense, bulk density about 0.9 g/ml. 385 ml x 0.9 ≈ 345 g. This is a generous estimate for a square slice of this thickness; a more conservative visible-dimension check (about 2.5-3 cm average height) gives ~250-290 g. I take about 300 g as the best estimate.

STEP 7 - Energy: Lasagna with meat sauce and cheese is roughly 140-160 kcal per 100 g cooked. Using 150 kcal/100 g: 300 g x 1.5 = 450 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single generous slab of lasagna on a side plate at about 300 g and roughly 450 kcal is plausible for a standard meal portion. The plate is not fully covered, so this is not an oversized serving.

Total: about 300 g, about 450 kcal.
